f.title: Treat a case as serious if it meets the seriousness criteria
f.statement: A serious adverse reaction or serious adverse event is an untoward medical occurrence that at any dose results in death, is life-threatening, requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongs existing hospitalisation, results in persistent or significant disability or incapacity, is a congenital anomaly or birth defect, or is judged to be a medically important event or reaction. This definition determines which reports fall under the 15-day timeline.
f.clause: Rule 2(xxxi). Definitions

rows.quote: "serious adverse reaction" or "serious adverse event" means an untoward medical occurrence that at any dose results in patient death, is life-threatening, requires inpatient hospitalization or results in prolongation of existing hospitalization, results in persistent or significant disability or incapacity, is a congenital anomaly or birth defect or is judged to be a medically important event or reaction;
rows.location: Rule 2(xxxi). Definitions
rows.review_note: Review: definition kept because it sets which reports are serious (15-day clock under rule 11(5)(a)); binding as part of statutory rules, so Mandatory. Double-check: quote and criteria list match.

f.title: Identify significant safety issues using the Rules' definition
f.statement: Significant safety issues include, but are not limited to: (a) modification or removal of an approved indication for safety reasons; (b) addition of a contraindication; (c) major changes to warnings, precautions or adverse reaction statements in the product information for safety reasons in any country where the product is marketed; (d) withdrawal or suspension of availability in another country based on signals; (e) issues identified by the registration holder through its own signal management process once the assessment is completed and actions are proposed; (f) significant safety results from post-marketing clinical studies; (g) safety issues due to misinformation in the product information; (h) safety issues related to use outside the product information or directions for use; (i) safety issues concerning the quality of raw materials; (j) a quality defect, adulteration, contamination or spurious product associated with a serious adverse reaction report; (k) issues for which the registration holder is considering sending a DHPC in any country where the product is marketed. These issues must be reported under rule 11(12).
f.clause: Rule 2(xxxiii). Definitions

rows.quote:
"significant safety issues" include but are not limited to-
 (a) modification or removal of an approved indication for safety reasons based on sound scientific evidence which was not scientifically established through clinical trials; (b) addition of a contraindication; (c) major changes to wamings, precautions or adverse reactions statements in the product information for safety reasons in any country where the therapeutic good is marketed; (d) withdrawal or suspension of availhbility of the therapeutio good in another country based on signals indicating seriousness and quality of information; (e) issues identified by the registration holder as a result of their own signal management process once the assessment has been completed and actions are proposed; (f) significant safety results from post-marketing clinical studies;
rows.location: Rule 2(xxxiii). Definitions
rows.review_note: Review: definition kept because it decides what triggers the 15-day significant safety issue report (rule 11(12)). Quote limited to items (a)-(f) for the 1000-character limit; items (g)-(k) are in the statement from the same list (text lines 204-218). Double-check: items (g)-(k) are not inside the quote, so below 90.

f.title: Report lack of efficacy for vaccines, contraceptives, antimicrobials and critical-care drugs within 15 days
f.statement: Lack of therapeutic efficacy with vaccines, contraceptives, antimicrobials and drugs used in critical conditions or life-threatening situations shall be reported to the NPC within fifteen calendar days in the DRAP-approved format.
